title: Prompt engineering: instructions, few-shot, and output contracts
summary: Write prompts that behave like reliable function calls: clear instructions, well-chosen examples, and an output shape your code can trust.

title: Context engineering: what actually goes into the window
summary: Prompt engineering asks how to phrase the request — context engineering asks what the model gets to see. The attention-budget mental model, the write/select/compress/isolate toolkit, and the five failure modes that break agents.

title: RAG architectures: naive, advanced, and when to skip RAG
summary: Don't teach the model your data — hand it the right pages at query time. Chunking, hybrid search, reranking, groundedness gates — and knowing when to skip RAG entirely.

title: Chunking and embeddings: the unglamorous 80%
summary: The two unglamorous decisions that determine 80% of retrieval quality: how you cut documents into self-contained chunks, and how you turn them into vectors. Cosine similarity as an angle, the one-model rule, and the token-level eval that keeps chunking honest.

title: Vector databases: indexes, ANN search, and trade-offs
summary: Your embeddings are points in space; finding the nearest ones is the retrieval problem. Why exact search dies at scale, how HNSW and IVF make ANN fast, and the recall–latency–memory triangle every index trades on.
